headline: Climate is weather averaged over time—patterns emerge that individual days obscure
universal_truth: Short-term variation hides long-term trends; zoom out to see the pattern
fun_facts: Climate is typically defined as weather patterns averaged over 30 years
The difference between ice ages and warm periods is only about 5°C average temperature
Earth's climate has been stable enough for civilization for about 10,000 years—an unusually calm period
discussion_questions: What patterns in your life only emerge over time?
How do daily fluctuations hide larger trends?
What would you see differently if you zoomed out?

hook.script: Today is sunny. Yesterday was rainy. Day-to-day weather seems random. But zoom out—average across years—and patterns emerge. Deserts stay dry. Tropics stay wet. Climate is the pattern that weather hides.

cliff.script: We often focus on immediate variation and miss underlying patterns. Weather changes daily; climate changes slowly. What does this distinction teach us?
cliff.prompt: What's the value of long-term patterns?

options.text: Long-term patterns reveal what short-term variation obscures—trends, cycles, and underlying dynamics that predict better than any single data point
options.response: Yes. One rainy day doesn't mean wet climate. One good quarter doesn't mean success trend. Zooming out reveals whether you're seeing noise or signal.

options.text: The present moment is what matters most
options.response: The present matters for action, but patterns help predict and plan...

fact1.title: Signal and Noise
fact1.script: Daily weather is noisy—variable, unpredictable. Climate is the signal within the noise—the average, the pattern. Separating signal from noise requires time and perspective.

fact2.title: Timeframe Matters
fact2.script: The pattern you see depends on how long you look. A week shows weather. A decade shows trends. A century shows cycles. The 'truth' changes with timeframe.

fact3.title: Personal Climate
fact3.script: Your life has weather and climate too. Daily moods fluctuate; underlying happiness is more stable. One bad day isn't a bad life. Zoom out to see your personal climate.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Short-term variation hides long-term trends. Zoom out to see the pattern. Don't confuse weather with climate—in nature or in life.

outro.script: That's Day 237. Tomorrow, we'll explore what's happening in the sky. Until then, look for a pattern in your life that daily variation obscures.

growTrack.title: Zoom Out - Find the Pattern
growTrack.learning_objective: Distinguish signal from noise through time perspective
growTrack.activity: Pick an area of life where you tend to react to daily variation—mood, finances, progress. Zoom out: what's the pattern over months or years? Is today's 'weather' actually representative of your 'climate'? Perspective reveals patterns.
